title: Kiroshi Overview & Purpose
content: Kiroshi is a Streamlit-based documentation cockpit for IT support engineers. It consolidates every input needed to describe a customer case, automates recap emails, and exports polished summaries. The homepage Dashboard surfaces tracked case status, Dell escalations, FedEx replacements, and recently saved work so you can triage at a glance. A persistent autosave file guards against data loss, and every case can be re-opened in a dedicated tab for multitasking.

title: Core Case Workflow
content: Open a case tab to document the engagement end-to-end. Fill the Case Details block with customer, subscription, and application information, then capture communication notes, remote access credentials, root cause analysis, and solutions. Toggle escalation fields when a second-line handoff is required, or enable hardware sections to log PC specifications, scanner serials, and warranty data. Upload screenshots and logs, capture images from screen selections, and bundle everything into a ZIP export alongside the generated PDF summary. The Tables tab produces an Excel-ready grid of every field, while the tracking switch writes priority, ticket numbers, and ETA information to the persistent database for Dashboard visibility.

title: AI Assistance & Reporting
content: Use the Verify and Categorizer tools to audit documentation quality, or Ask ATOM for guided answers with context awareness. AI Assist can draft recap emails or troubleshooting steps based on the captured data. Enabling AI Educate unlocks historical analytics: refresh the dataset from saved cases, review keyword and root-cause trends, merge collaborator knowledge bases, and download branded PDF reports. The Report tab also houses the Bug Detector to spot recurring failure patterns across your portfolio.

title: Configuration, Storage & Launch
content: Persistent settings live in the KiroshiDatabase directory under your user profile (or C:\ProgramFiles on Windows). Autosave.json stores the active workspace, while tracked cases are written to the TrackedCases folder for dashboard analytics. The application can be launched with `streamlit run case_documentation_app.py` or the bundled run_app.py helper, and packaged through build.sh for distribution. Environment variables such as AI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY control GPT connectivity, and manual reference notes feed the A.A.T.O.M. knowledge base. The onboarding tutorial records completion status in settings and can be replayed from the Settings tab.
